concerns.text: The scaffold is created under `projects/PROJ-001-assessing-statistical-power/` instead of the required `projects/PROJ-234-assessing-statistical-power-in-reproduci/`, violating the project identifier and the Single Source of Truth (SSoT) requirement.

`api_client.py` is described as a thin wrapper but the task does not require it to raise `DataFetchError` on bad URLs nor to implement exponential‑backoff; this weakens FR‑007 (real‑call testing) and FR‑001 (robust API access).

The ingestion script is specified to filter on a non‑existent `url` field, does not use the mandated `utils.api_client` wrapper, and produces an empty `filtered_datasets.json` with no schema‑validation test, leaving FR‑001 and FR‑002 uncovered.
FR‑012 is referenced in the assumptions and edge‑case discussion but is never defined in the specification, creating an orphan functional requirement.
FR‑016 and FR‑017 appear in the implementation plan and task list (e.g., T009, T010) but are absent from the specification, constituting undocumented scope creep.

The checksum manifest is written to `data/processed/checksum_manifest.json`, whereas the constitution and data model mandate a single SSoT file `data/metadata.json`; this violates Principle IV (SSoT).

`config.yaml` sets `max_runtime_hours: 6` and `max_memory_gb: 8`, conflicting with SC‑001a and SC‑003 which require a CI runtime limit of ≤ 214 minutes (≈ 3.6 hours) and SC‑004 which caps memory at 8 GB; the runtime limit is overstated.
The power‑calculation step omits the required clamping of power values > 1.0, contrary to the specification’s rule to clamp and log a warning.
Task T015 refactors OA logic into `code/utils/open_access.py` but earlier tasks and the plan still import `utils.oa_checker`, leaving dangling imports that will cause runtime errors.
